title: Measurement playbook: pick the study from the question

rows.question: Is this channel adding sales at all?
rows.method: Geo experiment (go-dark or heavy-up in matched regions)
rows.use_when: The channel can be switched off or raised by region; user-level holdouts are not possible or not trusted
rows.eligibility: PAWLY: 20 matched region pairs, 6 weeks, national budget of at least KRW 1.75M/day so that an iROAS of 1.0 is detectable (MDE 2.6% of revenue). A 30% go-dark share detects 0.75 at 59% of the revenue at risk
rows.output: Incremental revenue and iROAS with a 95% interval; brand-search lift as a second KPI
rows.watch_out: Spillover between regions, local promotions in control regions, budget changes during the test

rows.question: Our budget is below the geo-test threshold. What can we still learn?
rows.method: Platform conversion lift (user-level holdout), or a planned on/off period read with causal impact
rows.use_when: National budget for the channel under about KRW 1.75M/day, or fewer than ~20 comparable regions
rows.eligibility: Conversion lift: enough conversions per arm to meet the platform's minimum. On/off read: a stable pre-period and one clean change date
rows.output: A lift estimate with a wide interval; results pool into a calibrated MMM as the business grows
rows.watch_out: An underpowered test that reads 'no effect' when the honest answer is 'can't tell yet'

rows.question: We already paused or changed something. What did it do?
rows.use_when: A single, dated change happened and no holdout was planned
rows.eligibility: A stable pre-period several times longer than the post-period; control series that the change did not touch
rows.output: Day-by-day counterfactual and cumulative effect with a credible interval
rows.watch_out: Seasonality or promotions that coincide with the change; a simple before/after comparison absorbs them

rows.question: Reported conversions jumped after switching to AI auto-bidding. Is it real?
rows.method: Total-sales check around the switch (regression discontinuity in time + placebo dates)
rows.use_when: Platform-reported results rose but total sales did not obviously move
rows.eligibility: A clear switch date, daily total sales from the advertiser's own system, no other big change within about four weeks
rows.output: Split of the reported increase into true incremental sales and sales re-credited from brand search and organic
rows.watch_out: Attribution window changes; budget increases that follow the high reported ROAS

rows.question: Every platform says it drove the sale. Whose numbers do we believe?
rows.method: Cross-platform comparison: each platform's reported revenue vs incremental revenue
rows.use_when: Several platforms each report a strong ROAS and their claims add up to more than ads could have driven
rows.eligibility: Per-channel platform reports plus one incrementality source: an experiment or a calibrated MMM
rows.output: Credit ratio per channel (reported / incremental); headroom where platforms under-credit
rows.watch_out: Ranking channels by their own reported ROAS; attribution windows that differ by platform

rows.question: How should next year's budget be split?
rows.method: Bayesian media mix model calibrated with experiment results; response curves
rows.use_when: Several channels compete for one budget and spend varies over time
rows.eligibility: About two years of weekly data, real spend variation per channel, at least one experiment to calibrate against
rows.output: Channel response curves, marginal ROI and a reallocation with expected gain ranges
rows.watch_out: Channels whose spend moves together; without calibration the model can hand one channel's effect to another

rows.question: Did the campaign raise interest in the brand?
rows.method: Search lift (brand search volume as a KPI in the geo test) or a brand lift survey
rows.use_when: Upper-funnel goals; purchase effects may take longer than the test
rows.eligibility: PAWLY: the same 6-week geo design detects a 2.1% change in brand searches
rows.output: Lift in brand searches (or ad recall) with an interval
rows.watch_out: Brand search ads can steal clicks from organic results; measure searches, not ad clicks
